text: bun run pr open could not push a rebased branch (non-fast-forward). Fixed: --force pushes with --force-with-lease.
When the pre-push checks failed, bun run pr open said to use --force, as if a rebase caused it. Fixed: it says to read the git output and fix the check first.
bun run pr open counted an added .changeset/README.md as the changeset, so CL-032b got none. Fixed: it checks the basename.
validate sets CI=1 locally, so code that detects CI with the CI variable (snap screenshot compare) misfires in the pre-push hook; use GITHUB_ACTIONS
A commit whose first line is over 72 chars fails in the commit-msg hook after lint-staged ran, and a chained pr open then pushes without that commit
clutch issues new writes the issue file, then fails when oxfmt is missing (no bun install in a fresh worktree); a retry takes the next id, so two ids get used

design-proposal: the record names one prototype path, but a real prototype spans several (gallery group, board, wide-page switch, adopted page in the [group] route); check-proposals cannot see leftovers outside that one path

design-proposal Adopt step 4 says store the screenshots where visual review keeps baselines, but not how to make them: the board's frames do not match snap's geometry, so I built an adopted-direction page in the route's page template and shot it at 390 and 1280 by hand

design-proposal: nothing renders the real screen over the proposal's sample data, so the build-vs-spec compare needed a throwaway harness (real ApprovalScreen over a local pool); it could not be committed because it pushed the app over check-first-screen

design-proposal: ProposalBoard and the wide gallery page are per-project scaffolding that dies with the last proposal (knip, first-screen ratchet), so each proposal rebuilds them; the template should ship the board

design-proposal Create step: a direction drew data the screen cannot read (contractor name, change order number for a homeowner), found only at adoption; the skill should ask to check each shown field against the screen's records
design-proposal: the owner's brief answer lands in answers.json and nothing tells an agent to adopt; adoption ran only because a coordinator relayed it

design-proposal in a project behind on Clutch (Neighborhood on v0.44.2): the skill, check-proposals and visual review are all missing, so I ran Clutch's check-proposals from the Clutch checkout and seeded baselines with no snap to confirm them
tools/journeys/run.test.ts 'several web apps and no journeys.webApp' tests failed in CI's full bun test run on #202 (and likely #197) but pass alone and on main; order- or environment-dependent

CL-514 named C-Suite branch test-week-builds-stack, which no longer exists. stack.md on main names scorer, trigger and runner keys that differ from the CL-514 Design, so the lane had to compare both with C-Suite's live tree before it could pick keys.
Agent review on a stacked PR whose base lags main reviewed main's #194 babysit changes as if the PR added them, and raised 7 false owner findings on #207 and #208
GitHub REST core limit was 0 at 17:45 UTC (shared by 3 lanes); clutch score waited 30 min for the reset before the first real run

Bun fetch closes a response that sends no data for 300 s, so a non-streamed qwen3.8-27b judge call (8 tokens/s, long reasoning) failed as 'The operation timed out' despite a 1 h AbortSignal; fixed by streaming
Two lanes opened PRs on the same base within a minute, which broke the linear stack
A sync ran the project's old Clutch binary, so add_on_sync files needed a second run (CL-519)
clutch worktree new <slug> --issue CL-436 doubled the id into the branch (clutch/cl-436-cl-436-x) and ran issues set in the main checkout, which did not have the new issue file yet

apps/cli/src/factory/intake-doc.test.ts 'a section that names the same values as factory.intake passes' failed once in CI on #226 (run 42324940169): checkIntakeDoc saw no tracker README in a fresh mkdtemp repo. Passed on the next head. Root cause not found in 10 minutes.

Agent review re-posts the same owner findings as new threads on every push (#226 and #227 got 5-15 repeat threads per head), so a PR waiting on the owner burns babysit rounds until the 8-per-day cap marks it stuck. Agent review should skip an owner finding that an earlier thread on the same path already raised.
@repo/cli:test runs at 59 to 61 s against its 60 s budget on a Mac with other sessions running, so validate failed twice on the budget alone and passed on the third run

tools/lint/import-policy.mjs sits exactly at its 660-line budget, and a lint plugin cannot import a sibling module (Node does not resolve @tools/, and aliases-only rejects a relative path). Any new rule logic has to live in oxlint.config.ts or be copied. Give lint plugins one allowed way to share a helper.
Journey notes-sync failed, then passed on the retry, on web (Phone). See test-results/journeys/measures/notes-sync.json.

On a Mac whose only git is the /usr/bin shim, each git call costs about 8 ms against 3.7 ms for the real program. The CLI tests start thousands of them, so the suite sat at its 60-second budget and timed out under machine load, which refused a push. The CLI now finds the real git once. About 30 files under tools still call the shim.

The first run of the iOS app on an iOS 27 simulator closed at launch: iOS 27 requires the scene life cycle and the Expo 57 project template does not adopt it. Fixed with the config plugin apps/app/scene-lifecycle.cjs, to delete at Expo 58.

The native bundle of One 1.27.1 is one plain script, so a top-level variable of any module is a global that React Native and Expo cannot replace (File from Effect Schema, Event, TextDecoderStream and 30 more). The app opened on an error screen. apps/app/native-setup.ts now reserves the names by hand; a newer One may make that list unnecessary.

The native Screen of the design system gave className to SafeAreaView of react-native-safe-area-context, which react-native-css does not style, so each screen had no height on a device. No check saw it, because no journey had run on a device.

apps/cli/src/main.test.ts 'installation hands off to any interface without launching even a saved agent, and resumes each stage' timed out at its 5000 ms limit twice on 2026-11-12 under machine load, and passed on the next run each time. validate failed on it alone. The test needs about 5 seconds when the machine is idle, so it has no margin.
A native journey run left the app running in the simulator; it spun for five hours and pushed the CLI tests over their 60 second budget, so no push passed.
After each release, a stacked pull request conflicted with main in .clutch/TRACKER.md; a stack of nine stopped after its first merge.
The reach rule started the iOS lane for every sensitive path, and the judge held a pull request whose iOS job failed; together they held every change to the merge gate until CL-474.
The Playwright browser tool writes .playwright-mcp/ into the repository root, and oxfmt --check then fails validate on its .yml files.
GitHub updates the next pull request of a stack after a merge and drops its approval, so each pull request of a stack needed a new approval.

clutch issues --write in a branch rewrites .clutch/TRACKER.md, and nothing stops a commit of it. The release workflow owns that file, so a pull request that commits it conflicts with main after each merge. It cost six merges of main on 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14.
clutch issues new fails with 'Could not find oxfmt' in a fresh worktree until bun install runs. The message does not name the fix.

A pull request merges when its checks pass, often before agent review posts. On 2026-11-13 three blocking findings arrived after the merge (#262, #269, #270), and each needed a follow-up pull request.
pr findings reads only the newest Review disposition comment, so a second comment that answers one new finding makes each earlier finding show as unanswered.
